title: Carry / defensive sleeve and the blend
hypothesis: A carry/defensive sleeve, risk-parity blended with trend, beats either alone.
question: Does a long-only risk-parity income book with a yield-curve carry tilt diversify trend well enough to lift the blended Sharpe above 0.8?
prior: Carry earns a premium across asset classes (Koijen, Moskowitz, Pedersen and Vrugt 2018).
citations: Koijen, R., Moskowitz, T., Pedersen, L. H. & Vrugt, E. (2018). Carry. JFE 127(2).
method: Carry sleeve = long-only risk-parity book with a yield-curve tilt (^TNX/^IRX).
Sleeves blended by inverse vol with a Sharpe tilt, 10% floor, weights lagged one day.
verdict_reason: Trend and carry correlate +0.13. The blend reached Sharpe 0.84 on the full window (1.03 from 2007, once enough ETFs existed; see v33) and became the flagship.
lessons: The early pre-2007 years are thin (few ETFs existed); the diversified record starts ~2007.
footer: Research code is private; methods summarised below.
